subject.title: fix(irc): disconnect on oversized inbound lines

question: When a ready IRC connection receives an oversized inbound record, should OpenClaw discard that record and continue, or terminate the connection and enter a defined supervisor recovery path?
rationale: The IRC protocol permits multiple responses, while the current monitor lifecycle does not establish how an intentional post-ready socket close recovers; choosing this behavior affects compatibility and channel availability.

options.title: Close and recover
options.body: Keep the fail-closed disconnect, but propagate termination to the account lifecycle so status updates and reconnect-with-backoff behavior are explicit and tested.

options.title: Discard the record
options.body: Enter a bounded discard-until-delimiter state, report the protocol error, and preserve the connection for subsequent valid records.

options.title: Accept manual recovery
options.body: Merge the current disconnect behavior knowing an oversized record may leave the IRC account offline until an operator or process restart.

recommendation.title: Close and recover
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed disconnect, but propagate termination to the account lifecycle so status updates and reconnect-with-backoff behavior are explicit and tested.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository explicitly assigns IRC ownership to @vignesh07, and this choice defines IRC account lifecycle behavior.
